notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.12

Cloudflare sign-in
• Integrations → Cloudflare: one "Sign in with Cloudflare" in your browser. Read-only by default, and you choose the permissions on Cloudflare's page. Your agents can then use Cloudflare's own tools: your account through the Cloudflare API, plus Cloudflare's documentation.
• Searching and reading run freely. Anything that could change your account asks you first, every time, and deploys keep their own approval.
• Optional tools (Browser Run, Container, Agents SDK docs) are folded away behind a switch, with their billing or change warning shown when you turn one on.
• Sign out revokes the sign-in at Cloudflare. The sign-in is kept in your keychain and renews itself.
• Live checks of the Cloudflare AI recipes, opt-in per project on a test account. Each run needs your approval in the app. They run from your Mac, so no Cloudflare credential ever enters a build machine, and only checks that really passed against Cloudflare raise a recipe's evidence.
• Advanced: a narrow API token instead of the sign-in, checked with Cloudflare before it is kept.

Honest verification
• When nothing was agreed before Start, Vekrun now writes acceptance criteria from your request's own words, labelled "derived by Vekrun from the request", and checks them. The reviewer reads every change against them again, including single-agent runs.
• A run whose tests passed but where no acceptance criteria were checked now reads "Not verified", never "Verified", everywhere: the Work Item, its evidence and history. Accepting or delivering it asks for your reason, like any partly verified result.

Work Item fixes
• The bottom of a Work Item is no longer cut off by a dark band; the page fills the window and scrolls properly with or without a notice at the top.
• "What the goal likely touches" no longer shows a yellow warning about unlinked callers. It is one plain line naming the code, and words like "please" no longer match images or vendored files.
